classifications: Theory of computation → Pseudorandomness and derandomization
statement: We list here some of our favorite directions for future research: In Theorem 2, we showed that most degree ≤ d polynomials are sumset dispersers (in fact, extractors) for min-entropy k = O(dn1/⌊d/2⌋ ). On the other hand, we also know that no degree ≤ d polynomial is a sumset disperser for min-entropy k = c · dn1/(d−1) , where c > 0 is some constant. Can we narrow this gap? We conjecture that most degree ≤ d polynomials are sumset extractors with exponentially small error for min-entropy k = CdnC/d for some constant C > 0, even when d is a constant.17 We think that even showing this for small linear min-entropy would already be quite interesting. In the full version, we show that there exist (non-explicit) degree ≤ 4 low-error twosource extractors for any linear min-entropy via approximate duality [10]. This approach, √ however, provably cannot go below min-entropy n [9]. Can we show the existence of √ low-degree low-error two-source extractors for min-entropy below n?
